answer: A market for violet inventories and falcon observations admits each key only after it commits a uniquely encoded 10 GB file. Validators issue unpredictable block queries and verify Merkle proofs before granting a vote; missed audits suspend the key. Encoding binds every file to its key, preventing one copy from serving many aliases. Each extra identity needs more disk space throughout the epoch. Each parallel audit thread still needs a separate file. Security assumes queries arrive faster than attackers can regenerate missing blocks and storage costs exceed extra voting gains.
